english.title: Employer fail to keep copy of notice / data in relation to average hourly output rate
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being an employer of

(A)_[a worker]_
(B)_[workers]_

who did output work and to whom you had given a notice in accordance with regulation 41(1)(d) of the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015, failed to keep a copy of that notice and a copy of such data as was necessary to show how the average hourly output rate had been determined, for a period of six years beginning with the day upon which the pay reference period immediately following that to which it related ended
english.legislation: Contrary to regulation 59(4) and (8) of the National Minimum Wage Regulations 2015 and section 31(2) and (9) of the National Minimum Wage Act 1998.
english.pointstoprove:
Date and Location
employer of worker who did output work
reg 41(1)(d) notice given
failed to keep copy of notice and such data
as necessary to show how average hourly output rate had been determined
for period specified in reg 59(8)

investigatoraction.description: Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: (i) Where the worker in question qualifies for an agricultural minimum rate of wages, the records required to be kept under regulation 59(3), (4) and (5) are to be in a form which enables the information kept in respect of a pay reference period to be produced in a single document - Regulation 59(7)

other.penalty:
Summary: A fine not exceeding the statutory maximum
Indictment: A fine

Time Limit for Prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates' court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
